Subject: Private deployment upgrade: coordinating compatibility gates and evacuation cadence

Hi Logan / Monica,

We are lining up a maintenance window for our on-prem Redwood Private deployment (cluster: acme-nyc-pvt) to apply the 1.18.2 -> 1.19.0 runtime patch. Before we lock the date I wanted to confirm two things with the Redwood team:

1) Compatibility gates: can you share the matrix of model variants and quantization profiles that will be considered incompatible with 1.19.0? We need to validate our pinned model sets before the window.

2) Evacuation cadence and backout thresholds: what are the precise metrics (error rate / tail latency / CPU GPU memory pressure) you use to trigger an automatic backout vs. a manual abort? We have an internal SRE policy that requires numeric thresholds.

Proposed window: Tue Jun 22, 0200-0600 UTC (narrow maintenance window). Can Redwood support a staged canary (10% nodes -> 50% -> 100%) with a 30-minute observation at each step?

Attach anything helpful; we also need a short runbook so our compliance team can sign off.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Nguyen
Platform Engineer, AcmeCorp
SRE - NYC

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment upgrade: coordinating compatibility gates and evacuation cadence

Thanks for the heads-up, Tim — good questions. High level response and proposed plan below; attaching a compact compatibility matrix and the maintenance calendar (ICS) for the proposed window.

Summary (short):
- Compatibility gates: we classify incompatibility into "blocker" and "soft-filter". Blockers are ABI-level changes or quantization format differences (e.g., new 4-bit packing) that will fail model load. Soft-filters are performance regressions detected in canary. See attached compatibility-matrix.xlsx for specific model families.
- Evacuation cadence / backout thresholds (proposed):
  * Canary phases: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30-minute steady-state checks.
  * Automated abort (immediate rollback):
    - 5xx rate increase > 4x baseline sustained for 3m, OR
    - p99 latency increase > 2x baseline sustained for 5m, OR
    - GPU memory OOM events on >1 node in the canary tranche.
  * Manual abort (operator decision):
    - Quality drop (LM output divergence above agreed threshold for fixed prompt set), OR
    - Any outage affecting customer-facing route < 1 minute but repeated failures across multiple nodes.

Operational asks from AcmeCorp:
1) Confirm the narrow window (we can accommodate Tue Jun 22 0200-0600 UTC).
2) Share the pinned model list you intend to keep during the window (we'll run quick local compatibility checks against the matrix).
3) Provide access for our engineer to the post-upgrade telemetry stream (read-only).

I'll let Karthik include the exact runbook excerpt and the rollback commands we plan to use (so your compliance artifact can reference the specific steps).

Attachments: compatibility-matrix.xlsx, maintenance-calendar.ics

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.inference.com

--
Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference across hosted and private deployments

Adding the technical runbook excerpt and exact thresholds you asked for — pasted below for quick inclusion in your change packet. I'll also upload a one-page PDF and a short DocuSign flow after this message.

Runbook excerpt (abridged):
- Pre-checks (T-48h):
  * Validate pinned model checksums against compatibility-matrix.xlsx (MD5 list included).
  * Verify node drain grace = 300s, KV cache persist snapshot successful on canary nodes.
- Canary phase (10%):
  * Deploy runtime 1.19.0 to canary nodes (label: upg-canary-1).
  * Observation: record p50/p95/p99 latency and 5xx. Baseline numbers (your cluster): p95 = 210ms, p99 = 460ms, 5xx baseline = 0.12% (these are cluster-specific; we derived from last 14d).
  * Auto-rollback triggers (canary):
    - 5xx > 0.5% for 3 consecutive 60s windows OR
    - p99 > 920ms for 5m OR
    - Any OOM on GPU runtime observed in >0 nodes (immediate rollback).
- Escalation: engineer to open bridge and escalate to oncall if manual abort condition met.
- Rollback commands (operator):
  * redwoodctl rollout cancel --cluster acme-nyc-pvt --to-version 1.18.2
  * redwoodctl pin set --cluster acme-nyc-pvt --version 1.18.2 --reason "post-upgrade rollback"
  * Confirm KV cache restore: redwoodctl kv restore --cluster acme-nyc-pvt --snapshot latest-before-upgrade

Artifacts I'll attach after this email: runbook-onepage.pdf, docusign-change-link.txt (short link), and the script we use to compute output divergence (divergence-check.sh).

If that looks good I'll finalize the PDF and send for signing; please confirm the acceptance of the numeric thresholds above or propose tighter limits.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime & Orchestration, Redwood Inference
